title: Lewis Acids and Complex Ions
short: Metal ions accept electron pairs from ligands, and Kf measures how tightly the complex holds together.
trouble: Students think a Lewis acid must contain hydrogen, or that forming a complex ion makes a salt less soluble.

blocks.html: A lone pair can do more than sit on an atom: it can form a bond to something that has room for it. That broader idea of acids and bases explains why metal ions grab ammonia or cyanide, and why that makes some insoluble salts dissolve.

A Lewis base donates an electron pair; a Lewis acid accepts one. Metal ions are Lewis acids. A metal ion bonded to several Lewis bases (ligands) is a complex ion, such as $\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+}$. Its formation constant $K_f$ measures how tightly it holds together, and forming it can dissolve a salt: $K = K_{sp} \times K_f$.

$\mathrm{BF_3}$ has only six electrons around boron and an empty orbital, so it accepts the lone pair of $\mathrm{NH_3}$ with no proton involved. A metal ion's empty orbitals accept lone pairs the same way. When ammonia ties up $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ as $\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+}$, free $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ drops, $Q$ falls below $K_{sp}$ for AgCl, and more AgCl dissolves. Adding the two reactions multiplies their constants.

blocks.name: ch-lewis
blocks.cap: Ammonia's lone pair forms a new bond to boron. $\mathrm{NH_3}$ is the Lewis base and $\mathrm{BF_3}$ the Lewis acid; no hydrogen ion moves.

blocks.title: Dissolving AgCl in ammonia
blocks.q: $K_{sp}(\mathrm{AgCl}) = 1.8 \times 10^{-10}$ and $K_f(\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+}) = 1.7 \times 10^{7}$. Find the molar solubility of AgCl in $1.0\ \text{M}$ $\mathrm{NH_3}$.
blocks.a: $0.050\ \text{M}$, nearly 4000 times its solubility in water.

blocks.title: How little free metal ion is left
blocks.q: A solution has $0.010\ \text{M}$ silver, nearly all as $\mathrm{[Ag(NH_3)_2]^+}$, with $0.98\ \text{M}$ free $\mathrm{NH_3}$. Estimate $[\mathrm{Ag^+}]$.
steps: $[\mathrm{Ag^+}] = 6.1 \times 10^{-10}\ \text{M}$: almost every silver ion is tied up.

blocks.html: Thinking a Lewis acid must contain hydrogen, or that forming a complex ion makes a salt less soluble. $\mathrm{BF_3}$ and $\mathrm{Ag^+}$ are Lewis acids with no hydrogen at all, and complex formation pulls metal ions out of the solubility equilibrium, so more solid dissolves.
Photographic "fixer" (sodium thiosulfate) works this way: it dissolves the unexposed silver bromide as $\mathrm{[Ag(S_2O_3)_2]^{3-}}$.
